svg.title: Hit Count: score every tool, count wins, keep the top heads
svg.text: Hit Count: score every tool, count wins, keep the top heads
toy: 6 heads, 5 training queries, 4 tools; your run: 512 heads, 200 queries, 100 tools
per head and query: score every tool
per head: the tool it scores highest on each query, and the hit counter

g.text: Your rule (code3.py:83–85): on each training query, a head HITS if the correct tool gets its highest score.
P1 wants B. L0H2, L1H0 and L1H2 score B highest: three hits. L0H0 always picks A (the first tool), L0H1 always D (the last).
P2 wants A. L0H0 hits for free (it always says A); so do L1H0 and L1H2.
P3 wants C. L0H2, L1H0, L1H1 and L1H2 hit.
P4 wants D. L0H1 hits for free (it always says D); so do L1H0 and L1H1.
P5 wants B again. Only L1H0 and L1H2 hit.
Sort by hits (code3.py:107–108): L1H0 = 5, L1H2 = 4, … Keep the top k (k = 2 here; you kept 10 of 512).
Position-driven heads (always first / always last) hit only when the answer happens to sit there, so counting filters them out.
